causeEffect.externalCue: Knees overly flexed, hips behind ankles; no spray from ski tips — all spray from tails/heels
causeEffect.internalCue: Quads burning; feels like falling backward

causeEffect.externalCue: Shoulders rotate with the skis; no upper/lower separation
Huge static wedge; skis never turn across the hill
causeEffect.internalCue: Legs tired from pushing the wedge

causeEffect.externalCue: Skis never finish across the hill; Z-shaped tracks
causeEffect.internalCue: Speed builds between turns; feels out of control

causeEffect.externalCue: Persistent wedge on easy terrain; tense, rigid upper body
causeEffect.internalCue: Feels stuck, can't release the turn

drills.easier: Hold instructor's hands or poles planted for support.
drills.fallback: March in place with skis on (no slide) to build standing balance first.
drills.harder: Longer slides; add slight direction changes.
drills.howTo: On flat terrain, slide one ski forward a few inches, then the other. Alternate.
drills.name: Shuffle
drills.purpose: Get comfortable sliding; independent ski movement; balance.
drills.watchFor: Lifting skis instead of sliding; leaning back.

drills.howTo: Step the skis around in a small circle, one ski at a time.
drills.name: Step Around
drills.purpose: Reposition skis independently; develop balance and leg steering.
drills.watchFor: Crossing ski tips; big clumsy steps.

drills.fallback: Practice on flat ground stepping sideways first.
drills.howTo: Step the uphill ski up, bring the other ski to meet it. Repeat.
drills.name: Side Step
drills.purpose: Move safely across a slope; first feel of edges gripping.
drills.terrain: Very gentle slope, across the hill
drills.watchFor: Skis sliding downhill (not enough edge); facing downhill.

cues: Feel your shins on the front of your boots.
drills.fallback: Have student jump and land — the landing position IS athletic stance.
drills.harder: Bounce gently — stance should absorb it without losing balance.
drills.howTo: Ankles flexed, knees flexed, hips flexed, chest relatively upright, hands forward, eyes looking ahead, feet hip/shoulder width, weight centered, shins touching boot fronts.
drills.name: Athletic Stance Check
drills.purpose: Establish the centered stance everything else builds on.
drills.terrain: Flat or very gentle slope, stopped
drills.watchFor: Standing straight-legged; hips behind heels; hands at sides/behind.

cues: Let them go — just a little.
drills.easier: Shorter glide; instructor alongside holding a pole for the student.
drills.fallback: Back to D1/D4 on flat until the sliding feeling is comfortable.
drills.howTo: Athletic stance, skis pointed downhill, glide a short distance, stop via terrain. Keep first glides very short.
drills.name: Straight Glide
drills.purpose: Feel skis moving while staying in control; first sliding sensation.
drills.terrain: Very gentle slope with flat runout
drills.watchFor: Panic braking with a huge wedge; leaning back as speed builds.

drills.howTo: Glide → let skis travel toward flatter/uphill terrain → slow → stop naturally.
drills.name: Glide to Uphill Stop
drills.purpose: Learn that terrain stops you — no panic needed when skis move.
drills.watchFor: Trying to stop with the body instead of letting terrain work.

drills.fallback: "Turn your feet" phrasing; demonstrate the foot movement without skis.
drills.howTo: Tips closer, tails apart — "small pizza." Cue the feet, not the push: "Turn your feet so the tips come toward each other." Start small.
drills.name: Wedge Stop
drills.watchFor: Shoving skis apart with straight legs; wedge so big they stop dead and lose balance; leaning back.

drills.fallback: D7 until a small wedge is reliable.
drills.howTo: "Show me a little pizza." Glide. "Make it bigger." Glide. "Smaller." Glide. "Now stop." Repeat.
drills.name: Wedge Size Game
drills.purpose: Teach the wedge as an adjustable dial, not an on/off brake.

cues: Too fast? Turn more across the hill.
drills.easier: Start the turn earlier; gentler terrain.
drills.fallback: D11 J-turns (more structured version of the same idea).
drills.harder: Start turns from a straight glide at slightly more speed.
drills.howTo: Glide → turn one direction → let the turn finish across the hill → stop. Then the other direction.
drills.name: One-Direction Turn to Stop
drills.purpose: First discovery that a turn controls speed.
drills.terrain: Gentle slope with room to turn across the hill
drills.watchFor: Turning with the whole upper body; not finishing the turn across the hill.

drills.fallback: D9; or instructor skis in front (D12) to give a visual track to follow.
drills.howTo: Short straight glide → gradually steer one direction → keep turning until skis point across/slightly uphill → stop. Track looks like a J. Both directions.
drills.name: J-Turns
drills.progression: J1 large → J2 smaller → J3 alternate directions → J4 rhythm (L-stop-R-stop-L…).
drills.purpose: Deliberate steering; turn completion; speed control without braking.
drills.watchFor: Rotating the entire upper body; stopping the turn halfway (skis still pointing downhill).

drills.fallback: D10 J-turns with the instructor demonstrating each one first.
drills.howTo: Instructor skis directly ahead making large, slow, obvious turns. "Follow my skis."
drills.name: Follow My Skis
drills.purpose: Learn turn shape by mirroring; takes verbal instruction out of the loop.
drills.watchFor: Student fixating on the instructor's back instead of the track; falling behind.

drills.howTo: Partial turns without fully changing direction: across the hill → slightly downhill → back across. Repeat several times one direction, then switch.
drills.name: Garlands
drills.purpose: Bridge between J-turns and linked turns; practice initiation and completion without committing to a full direction change.
drills.watchFor: Accidentally completing into a full turn (fine — that's progress); rushing.

cues: Finish the turn… now the other way.
drills.easier: Keep the stop between turns longer.
drills.fallback: D12 Garlands, or D10 J-turns alternating directions.
drills.harder: Remove the stop; add turn-shape variation (D14 concept).
drills.howTo: Turn left → across the hill → (stop at first) → turn right → across → stop. Gradually remove the full stop: L → R → L → R. Pausing between turns is fine — control over speed.
drills.name: Linked Wedge Turns
drills.watchFor: Rushing the transition; incomplete turns leading to a straight downhill run.

cues: Your turn IS your speed control.
drills.fallback: D8 Wedge Size Game (the adjustable-dial idea, transferred to turn shape).
drills.howTo: Same turn, two shapes: round turn finishing well across the hill vs. turn that points downhill longer. Feel the speed difference.
drills.name: Turn Shape Controls Speed
drills.purpose: The core Day-1 insight: turn shape, not braking, is speed control.
drills.watchFor: Student reverting to wedge-braking instead of shaping the turn.

drills.fallback: Skip it — not required on Day 1.
drills.howTo: Keep skis parallel and glide; tiny foot movements.
drills.name: Parallel Glide
drills.purpose: Show that skis can move and be steered while parallel. NOT a Day-1 requirement.
drills.watchFor: Pushing into a wedge from habit; tension.

drills.howTo: Cue only: "Hands forward." Alternatives: "Carry a pizza." "Hold a tray."
drills.name: Hands Forward
drills.purpose: Fix back-seat stance, rotating shoulders, waving arms.
drills.watchFor: Hands forward but hips still back (then use D17).

drills.howTo: "Feel your shins against the front of your boots."
drills.name: Feel the Boot
drills.purpose: Fix sitting back via ankle flexion, not chest-throwing.
drills.watchFor: Student throwing chest forward instead of flexing ankles.

drills.easier: Steps on flat first, then in a traverse.
drills.fallback: D1 Shuffle (same foot activity, no turn involved).
drills.howTo: Once basic wedge turns work: "Take little steps while you're turning" — small alternating steps with the skis through the turn.
drills.name: Thousand Steps
drills.purpose: Active feet, better balance, independent leg movement, less whole-body lean.
drills.watchFor: Steps so big they disrupt the turn; stopping the turn to step.
